### Overview

We currently don't run the kubernetes executor integration tests which can cause us to miss bugs since not everybody runs the  integration tests locally before pushing and some functionality isn't covered by unit tests.

For example #25767 would have been caught.

This is also an important step in making the kubernetes executor first class. 

### Proposal

1. [x] Run all kubernetes tests inside of CI talking to a kuberentes cluster. :point_right: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/merge_requests/2155
1. [ ]  Add to [code coverage
  count](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/c7438d7fb8e260956e1215e7a991d61016f4b483/.gitlab/ci/coverage.gitlab-ci.yml#L8-20)
1. [ ] Add tests to [junit
  report](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/c7438d7fb8e260956e1215e7a991d61016f4b483/.gitlab/ci/coverage.gitlab-ci.yml#L22-33)
1. [ ] Only run the integration tests with a build tag as proposed in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/issues/25768#note_345944558 so that the unit tests run as part of the `unit test` job and only integration tests run inside of this job.
title: Run kubernetes executor integration tests on GitLab CI

## Summary

When using services:alias with the docker executor with 2 or more services using the same image, the runner produces a warning which suggests that the services or aliases would not work:

`WARNING: Service <image_name> is already created. Ignoring.`

While explicit aliases work as intended (services can be access with those names), the aliases derived from the container images will overlap, produce this warning for the 2nd service, and will only use the derived alias for the 1st service.

## Description

We would like to be able to run ci/cd jobs on Windows ARM64, using docker-windows-executor. We have been using docker on windows arm64, with process isolation.

The problem is that whilst AMD64 binaries can run on Windows ARM64, it appears when a AMD64 based docker image is cannot load on windows ARM64. Whilst the AMD64 gitlab-runner binary appears to work on ARM64, the docker-windows-executor will load a servercore2022 (amd64) based docker image, and the job will fail. The following error is reported:

```shell
sha256:<redacted>
ERROR: Job failed (system failure): prepare environment: Error response from daemon: container <redacted> encountered an error during hcs::System::Start: failure in a Windows system call: The virtual machine or container exited unexpectedly. (0xc0370106) (exec.go:72:0s). Check https://docs.gitlab.com/runner/shells/#shell-profile-loading for more information
```

I have noticed that `The virtual machine or container exited unexpectedly` error message occurs when attempting to load a AMD64 image.

## Proposal

Microsoft does provide base ARM64 docker images, ltsc2025-arm64. See https://github.com/microsoft/Windows-Containers/issues/586, https://mcr.microsoft.com/v2/windows/nanoserver/tags/list, https://mcr.microsoft.com/v2/windows/servercore/tags/list

Current workaround used is to build a custom helper-image based on servercore:ltsc2025-arm64, and this works.

The minimum required change is to provide a helper-image that is based on ltsc2025-arm64. Customers can then override their runner settings to point to this image. Further changes would be helpful are:

* Build and use an ARM64 based helper.exe within the helper-image. Also use ARM64 based git, git-lfs and pwsh (the latter two should be easy, but using arm-based git requires an upgrade to a newer version of git that what is currently used)
  * Depends on [https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/ci-cd/runner-tools/base-images/](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/ci-cd/runner-tools/base-images/-/tree/main?ref_type=heads) updating to providing ltsc2025-arm64 variant of the base-image.
* Provide an ARM64 based gitlab-runner.exe
* Automatically detect that the runner is running on an ARM64 machine and use the appropriate image.

## Links to related issues and merge requests / references

<!--Please paste a link of the related issues or/and merge requests-->
title: Docker-windows-executor runner support for Windows ARM64

> **Triage note.** This report describes two defects with separate causes. The third section, "Running as a service with legacy process strategy", is split out to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/issues/39720 and is fixed separately.
>
> - https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/issues/39720 — with the flag set, the event reaches the process, then the runner force-kills it anyway. The runner reads the failure to restore its own console as a failed termination. Fix: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/merge_requests/7275
> - **This issue** — on the default path the event is never delivered, because a runner started by the Service Control Manager holds no console. Fix: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/merge_requests/7276, which routes the event through the console of the job process rather than one the runner does not have.
>
> Both are in 19.4. https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/issues/39721 adds the missing test coverage. https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/issues/39684 tracks the set.
>
> The report below is unchanged.

---

When running gitlab-runner as a Windows service, the runner process has no console, causing the graceful termination mechanism(s) to fail.

* gitlab-runner version: 17.11.1  (but newer versions behave the same)
* `executor = "shell"`
* `shell = "pwsh"`
* Windows version: 10.0.26100.7840

## Running interactively

If I run gitlab-runner from a console, there is a console, and the application being run is terminated gracefully.

```
Starting test run...
Canceling test run...
The test run was canceled.
WARNING: script canceled externally (UI, API)
```

(`WARNING` messages come from the runner; other messages come from the application being run by the script.)

## Running as a service

If I run gitlab-runner as a Windows service, there is no console, the application being run does not receive a signal to terminate, and the runner always kills the application immediately after it determines that graceful termination has failed.

```
Starting test run...
WARNING: Failed to terminate process: 1 error occurred:
	* failed to send Ctrl-Break event to process being terminated: The handle is invalid.
WARNING: script canceled externally (UI, API)
```

`GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent` fails.

## Running as a service with legacy process strategy

If I run gitlab-runner as a Windows service and configure the runner with `FF_USE_WINDOWS_LEGACY_PROCESS_STRATEGY = true`, there is no console, but the application being run *does* receive a signal to terminate gracefully and may terminate gracefully if it manages to do so before the runner kills it immediately after (incorrectly) determining that graceful termination has failed.

```
Starting test run...
WARNING: Failed to terminate process: 1 error occurred:
	* failed to attach the runner process to the console of its parent process: The handle is invalid.
Canceling test run...
The test run was canceled.
WARNING: script canceled externally (UI, API)
```

`AttachConsole` fails to reattach to the console of the runner's parent process.

Interestingly, `AttachConsole` does not fail to attach to the console of the process running the application, so this mechanism would work if it didn't go on to kill the process immediately afterward.
title: Canceling job always results in process kill when running as a Windows service

## Description

Currently, when registering a runner with the Docker executor using the `gitlab-runner register` command, there is no option to configure the Docker `pull_policy` directly via CLI parameters.

The only way to set this value is to manually modify the `config.toml` file after the runner has already been registered.

This makes it difficult to fully automate runner provisioning.

## Problem to solve

When provisioning runners automatically (for example using Docker containers, infrastructure automation, or scripts), all configuration should ideally be set during the `gitlab-runner register` process.

At the moment, the Docker pull policy can only be configured manually in `config.toml`. Example configuration:

`[runners.docker]`\
`pull_policy = ["if-not-present"]`

This requires an additional configuration step after registration, which complicates automated setups.

## Proposal

Please add a CLI parameter to the `gitlab-runner register` command that allows configuring the Docker pull policy during registration.

For example:

`gitlab-runner register `\
`--url "``https://gitlab.com/``" `\
`--registration-token "" `\
`--executor docker `\
`--docker-image docker:20.10.24 `\
`--docker-volumes /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock `\
`--docker-pull-policy if-not-present`

The command would then generate the corresponding entry in config.toml:

`[runners.docker]`\
`pull_policy = ["if-not-present"]`
title: Allow setting docker pull_policy via gitlab-runner register CLI

## Context

Part of a broader effort to make the Infra-attributable Error Rate SLI meaningful and actionable for Runner-side issues, without repeating the regression from !5715 (canceled jobs being counted as `runner_system_failure` and inflating infra alerts).

Related to: gitlab-org/gitlab#596251

## Objective

Enumerate all points in the runner code where a job is failed or a `BuildError` is returned, and record:

- The executor (`shell`, `docker`, `kubernetes`, `ssh`, `step-runner`, etc.) or whether it is executor-agnostic shared logic.
- The stage (e.g., `prepare`, `get_sources`, `restore_cache`, `download_artifacts`, script execution, `archive_cache`, `upload_artifacts`).
- The current `JobFailureReason` (if any) and exit code.
- Whether the path can be hit in:
  - Normal execution failure
  - User cancellation
  - Timeout or lost runner
  - Mixed cases (e.g., race between cancel and a failing stage, like the scenario that triggered !5715)

## Deliverables

A table or spreadsheet-like document listing, per executor and stage:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Code location | File + function |
| Error type / message | The error or `BuildError` returned |
| Current `JobFailureReason` | As set today |
| Failure attribution | Runner infra / GitLab/Rails/API/network infra / User config or environment / Ambiguous |

This gives us the raw data needed to redesign the taxonomy in the follow-on issue.

## Background

Today:
- Runner's use of `JobFailureReason` is inconsistent and sometimes overly coarse (`runner_system_failure` as a catch-all).
- Some truly user-caused or ambiguous failures end up classified as infra, which inflates the infra error rate and triggers noisy alerting.
- Cancel/timeout flows are interleaved with genuine infra failures in ways that make correct classification hard.
title: Systematic Audit of Failure Reasons in gitlab-runner

## Context

Part of a broader effort to make the Infra-attributable Error Rate SLI meaningful and actionable for Runner-side issues, without repeating the regression from !5715.

Related to: gitlab-org/gitlab#596251

Depends on the audit completed in the preceding issue (Systematic Audit of Failure Reasons in gitlab-runner).

## Objective

Define a clearer set of failure reasons that:

- Separates infra-attributable from user-driven failures where we have enough information.
- Keeps a small number of "ambiguous" or "other" codes for cases we really cannot disambiguate.
- Maps cleanly to Rails' failure reason enums and to the SLI dashboards.
- Correctly captures request failures against 3rd party services like DockerHub and GitHub repo clones.

## Proposed Top-Level Buckets

Working names to refine with CI/Pipeline Execution:

### `RunnerInfraFailure`
Hard failures in runner host or executor environment:
- Executor binary missing/broken.
- Runner not able to spawn containers/VMs/Pods.
- Internal runner bugs that stop the job from running correctly.

_Intention: clearly infra-attributable to Runner._

### `GitLabInfraOrNetworkFailure`
Failures due to:
- GitLab API 5xx errors.
- Network connectivity issues between runner and GitLab.
- SCM fetch failures clearly caused by GitLab side being unavailable.

_Intention: infra-attributable to GitLab backend rather than user code._

### `UserConfigurationFailure`
Misconfigurations, invalid options, unsupported features, e.g.:
- Invalid `GIT_CLONE_PATH` or `builds_dir`/`cache_dir` settings.
- Missing container image, invalid Kubernetes namespace, etc.

_Intention: excluded from infra-attributable error SLI._

### `UserEnvironmentFailure`
Failures where the job environment is under user control:
- Custom scripts that fail to prepare environment.
- User-managed dependencies not present or misconfigured.
- Non-zero exit codes from the script itself.

_Intention: user-code failures, also excluded from infra SLI._

### `Canceled / Timeout / LostRunner`
- Explicit cancellations initiated by users or API.
- Timeouts where the job exceeded configured time and runner reported timeout.
- Jobs where the runner goes away in a way we can reliably detect as infra.

_Intention:_
- _User-initiated cancel: not infra-attributable._
- _"Lost runner" or timeout due to infra: infra-attributable, but carefully defined to avoid races._

### `UnknownOrAmbiguousFailure`
Cases where we truly cannot distinguish between user and infra causes with current data. Kept as a small, explicitly tracked bucket.

_Intention: decide whether it belongs in the infra SLI or a separate "unclear" metric._

## Rails-Side Mapping and Dashboards

For every proposed runner failure reason, define:

- Corresponding Rails enum / database representation (e.g., values in `failure_reason`).
- Which panel/SLI bucket it contributes to:
  - Infra-attributable error rate (and whether it is clearly Runner vs Rails)
  - User-code failure rate
  - Ambiguous bucket for anomaly detection only

We should work closely with Pedro / Pipeline Execution and SLI owners to:
- Align on which failure reasons are counted in "infra-attributable errors" vs excluded as user-code.
- Ensure existing dashboards and alerts (including hosted runner alerts that hinge on `runner_system_failure`) are updated to the new mapping and semantics, not just the raw codes.

## Deliverables

- A short spec doc or table:
  - `Runner JobFailureReason` → Rails enum value → SLI bucket (Runner infra / GitLab infra / user-code / ambiguous)
- Clear note on how this changes:
  - The Grafana panels for infra-attributable error rate.
  - Runner-specific error-budget and alerting dashboards.
title: Design a Revised Failure-Reason Taxonomy and Rails Mapping

## Objective

Validate that the new taxonomy improves the Infra-attributable Error Rate SLI and Runner alerting in practice.

## Validation Criteria

Confirm:

- Infra SLI drops user/misclassified failures while still catching real Runner infra incidents.
- CI dashboards still have the visibility they need into:
  - All failure reasons for regression detection.
  - Runner-specific subsets for their own analysis.

Adjust the taxonomy or mappings if:
- We discover categories are too coarse.
- We are still double-counting ambiguous cases in infra metrics.

## Stakeholder Coordination

Work with Pedro / Pipeline Execution and SLI owners to:

- Review updated Grafana panels for infra-attributable error rate.
- Review Runner-specific error-budget and alerting dashboards.
- Confirm hosted runner alerts (which previously hinged on `runner_system_failure`) are correctly firing on the new mapping.
- Sign off that the new taxonomy does not introduce new blind spots in anomaly detection.
